column7: Acts 13:20, in context Acts 13:17-21 (tracked Douay-Rheims)
column10: The stored relative.statement was a reordering the tracked Douay does not contain, which attached the four hundred and fifty years to the judges - exactly the attachment the claim's own note denies (failure mode 15.1(1)). The statement is restored to the Douay's own word order (edited under A2-029, which owns that block) and the label now carries the whole verse verbatim instead of the leading clause alone, so the display no longer asserts the punctuation the note disclaims.
column11: A regression asserting that every relative.statement in events.yaml that quotes a Scripture verse is a substring-preserving quotation of the tracked Douay would have caught this; not authored here.
column13: OVERLAP: three findings touch israel.judges.period. A2-026 owns the claim note and the label; A2-029 owns the relative.of + relative.statement block; LEAD-015 owns the event-level note. The three old-strings are disjoint, so they may be applied in any order. The claim is NOT re-typed as duration: the Douay's word order puts the four hundred and fifty years before the judges are mentioned, so a duration of 450 years on this subject would assert the length the note denies. See LEAD-015 notes.

column7: Acts 13:19-21 (tracked Douay-Rheims)
column10: israel.monarchy.saul-accession is the period's terminus, not its origin: Saul enters only at v.21, after the judges. The anchor is moved to israel.conquest.division-of-the-land, which is what the verse's own 'after these things' names (v.19, the destroying of seven nations and the dividing of their land by lot), and the statement is restored to the Douay's word order. This is a sequence statement carrying no offset, the same shape israel.conquest.division-of-the-land and israel.judges.ark-comes-to-cariathiarim already use correctly.
column13: Removing this anchor also dissolves the LEAD-015 chain: demand-for-a-king -> judges.period no longer reaches saul-accession (a modern-critical 1020 B.C. the profile marks alternate and declines to display). The new anchor is forward-directed - division-of-the-land -> war-against-the-kings-of-chanaan -> crossing-of-the-jordan - and introduces no cycle. OVERLAP: see A2-026 notes.

column7: Haydock, artifact PDF page 430 (printed p. 400), note on 2 Kings 15 ver. 7; 2 Kings (2 Samuel) 15:7
column10: The anchor israel.monarchy.david-reign is an origin no inspected source proposes. Haydock names two rival origins, Vatable's (the people's petition for a king) and Salien's (David's first anointing), neither of which is Scripture's and neither of which this profile may adopt as its own (guidance section 4.3). The anchor is therefore moved to israel.monarchy.absalom-preparations - the chapter's own antecedent, which the same Haydock page separates from verse 7 by its year markers - and carries sequence only; the statement becomes the verse verbatim, and the note records both reported origins and the four/forty manuscript problem in the commentators' own voices. The Haydock passage record is added to sources, because the note characterises it (failure mode 15.1(4)) and previously did so without naming it.
column13: The pre-existing note said Haydock 'cites Salien and Usher'; page 430 in fact names Vatable and Salien for the origin of the forty and Kennicott, Grotius, Josephus and Theodoret for the four/forty problem, with Salien and Usher named only as chronologies that 'explain it well enough'. Corrected. If the lead prefers the audit's optional improvement, adding the word 'four' explicitly to the note is safe; I have quoted Haydock's own sentence instead. The alternate claim on this event (Haydock's A.M. 2980 / A.C. 1024 marker) is untouched.

column7: Van Hoonacker, "Book of Nehemiah", Catholic Encyclopedia vol. 10 (New York, 1911), section 1 (1)-(2); 2 Esdras (Nehemias) 1:1
column10: The claim's own note asserted that the corpus holds no first year of Artaxerxes to count the twentieth year from; the registered source prints the reign as 'Artaxerxes I (B. C. 465-24)' in its own voice, so the premise was false and the substituted anchor (an interval of 485-424 B.C. covering two reigns) gave the regnal year no determinate origin. A minimal new event israel.restoration.reign-of-artaxerxes-i is authored from that printed span, and the tidings are re-anchored on it so the twentieth year is measured from the first year of the king.
column13: AUTHORS ONE NEW EVENT. It is the smallest identity the sources require and is precedented: apostolic-age.accession-of-vespasian is held on exactly the same ground ('Held only because it is the anchor of the patristic reckoning'). Nothing else is authored around it: no Persian king list, no A.D./B.C. conversion, and the article's own B.C. 445 for the mission is explicitly refused in the new event's note because Van Hoonacker grounds it on 'the opinion of most historians of Israel' plus the Elephantine papyri (guidance section 4.3, failure mode 15.1(3)). If the lead declines the new event, the fallback is to keep relative.statement as a sequence about the calamity and leave the regnal number in the label only; but then the corpus keeps a numbered regnal offset with no origin, which is what the finding is about. NOTE: israel.restoration.nehemias-mission and any other claim counting Artaxerxes' regnal years should be checked against the new anchor by whoever owns them - I have not touched them.

column10: Exodus 7:25 measures the seven days from the striking of the river, not from the audience of Exodus 5, so anchor plus stored clause asserted an interval Scripture does not state (failure mode 15.1(2)). The seven days are removed from relative.statement and from the label and carried in the note as the interval inside the series that they are; the anchor israel.exodus.moses-before-pharao is kept, because it is where the series itself opens, and the statement and label now say only that. Exodus 5:1 and 12:29 are added to sources because the statement now quotes them.
column13: The audit's first option - author the striking of the river and anchor the seven days on it - is NOT taken, and should not be: the claim's subject is the whole ten-plague series, so 'seven days after the river was struck' would be a false date for the series whichever anchor carried it. The seven days belong to an event this corpus does not hold; the smallest identity that would carry them is israel.exodus.first-plague-the-river-struck (Exodus 7:20-21, 7:25), with the seven days then belonging to the SECOND plague rather than to this subject. I have not authored it, because it would need a second event for the second plague to be the thing the seven days date.

column7: Exodus 15:22; Numbers 33:3-8; Exodus 14:21-22
column10: Both cited verses count the three days from the passage of the Red Sea, while the claim anchored them on the Exodus itself, with Soccoth, Etham, Phihahiroth and the sea standing in between (failure mode 15.1(2)). A minimal new event israel.exodus.passage-of-the-red-sea is authored from Exodus 14:21-22 and Numbers 33:8 - itself a bare sequence relative to the Exodus, carrying no length and no era - and the three days are re-anchored on it.
column13: AUTHORS ONE NEW EVENT, which is the anchor the audit names and the smallest identity the sources require; no chronology is authored around it - no year, month or day, and no length for the passage. It is inserted immediately before the '# --- The wilderness' comment so it stays in the exodus group. It is NOT bound to any locus here: binding Ex 14 to it is a separate decision for whoever owns bindings.yaml, and until then it is an anchor only. ALTERNATIVE the lead may prefer, if a new event is unwelcome: re-type this claim as precision duration, days: 3, statement 'they marched three days through the wilderness, and found no water', since three days is a whole positive length of the march and no anchor is then needed; I did not choose it because the subject also covers the encampment at Elim, whose length Scripture does not give, so a bare three-day duration would understate the subject.

column7: Ezechiel 24:15-18; guidance/scripture-chronology.md section 10 (the PRECISIONS table) and section 10.0
column10: The recommendation - drop relative.of and carry the containment on the parent alone - is not expressible in the model. PRECISIONS is closed and holds no containment shape for a point event; duration.within exists only on a duration, and this episode has no stated length; and an event must carry a non-empty dates list, so dropping the claim would mean deleting the event and orphaning its bindings, losing verbatim Scripture testimony. The stored claim carries NO offset: its statement is the within-day sequence 'So I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening', so section 15.1(2) does not bite - nothing is measured from the ministry and nothing false is displayed. That is the same shape israel.judges.ark-comes-to-cariathiarim and israel.conquest.division-of-the-land already use correctly for an unquantified position.
column13: This is the family the brief says adversarial verification refuted - a finding asking for a shape the model does not hold - and I am not re-raising it. The claim's refusal to borrow the Ezech. 24:1 dateline is correct and stands, and its note already states the containment in terms ('anchored to the ministry and to nothing narrower, because nothing narrower is stated'). If a maintainer ever wants Date.anchor to stop returning a container for this shape, that is a model change (a containment precision, or a relative.note convention read by the query), not a data correction, and it should be raised against guidance section 10.0 rather than against this claim.

column13: MY MISTAKE, AND IT IS LIVE IN THE WORKING TREE. The correction itself applied correctly — the Maon note is rewritten and the new Absalom binding on Ps 30 exists — but the insertion edit in the first draft of this file mis-set its own boundaries and did two pieces of damage that the two edits above repair. (1) It emitted a ` sources:` line that the block it replaced did not contain, so ` sources:` now stands TWICE above the Ps 30 Maon source list; YAML takes the later key and `validate` passes, which is exactly why this needs fixing by hand rather than by a gate. (2) It stopped one line short and DELETED ` - {book: Ps, chapter: 70}` from the scope of the pre-existing Ps 62 + Ps 70 binding to the flight from Absalom. Confirmed live: `query Ps.70.1` now returns only the first-captivity superscription-setting, and its own note still discusses Ps 70 at length. Apply both repairs before anything else in this element is reviewed. The first repair's anchor is the doubled ` sources:` pair itself; the second restores the scope line and is anchored on the `- {book: Ps, chapter: 62}` scope entry and the note line that follows it. SUBSTANCE, for the cold reviewer: the page's long sentence is quoted in `evidence_quote` with the OCR's line-break hyphen in "see-ing" closed up and its "8, Chrys." read as "S. Chrys.", which is why the new binding itself quotes only the short clause "though some refer this psalm to the conspiracy of Absalom, (Theod. M.)", which the OCR carries cleanly. Two `preferred` lines on one psalm is not a loader error: section 4.4's rule is one preferred per SUBJECT per profile and these are two subjects; the mutual exclusivity is carried in the two notes, which is the only place a binding can carry it.

column11: tools/tpt scripture-chronology validate; tools/tpt scripture-chronology query Ex.12.41
column13: I did NOT follow the finding's recommendation to make 1490 the preferred claim. Sec. 4.2 puts Scripture at rank 1 and the encyclopedia at rank 6, and Sec. 4.4 makes `preferred` require a strictly higher rank than every alternate; 1490 is the encyclopedia's arithmetic FROM 3 Kings 6:1 plus Ussher's regnal years, so preferring it would put a rank-6 report of Ussher above the rank-1 verse it is computed from. The corpus already resolves the identical pair the other way on israel.monarchy.temple-begun, where 3 Kings 6:1 is preferred and the same sentence's 1010 is alternate. E1-010 carries the matching preferred edit; this finding and E1-010 must land together or the subject loads with no preferred and no disputed claim (Sec. 4.4). Overlaps E1-009, E1-010, LEAD-014, P-004 on the same event; all `old` strings are disjoint.

column7: Howlett, "Biblical Chronology", closing sentence of "The Exodus to the building of Solomon's Temple" (retained text line 168; src.py line 174)
column10: The 'about 1277' claim is removed from catholic-traditional-v1 entirely. It is Howlett's own Egyptological reconstruction, reached on Sayce's Ramses II dates, Driver, and Wellhausen's and Stade's treatment of 3 Kings 6:1 as a late insertion; the article itself says 'This is not the traditional date of the Exodus'. profiles.yaml's second non-authority names exactly this class and says it is 'Not consulted', and Sec. 4.1 makes a modern chronology a separate profile with its own id. The boundary is preserved in the subject note (LEAD-014's edit), not as a claim.
column11: tools/tpt scripture-chronology validate; tools/tpt scripture-chronology query Ex.12.41
column13: Removing the claim, not re-disposing it, because Sec. 4.3's reporting licence is granted to Ussher alone ('may be reported where a ranked Catholic source itself prints his figures') and expressly NOT to modern critical chronology. An `alternate` would still be a modern figure consulted inside this profile. Re-profiling it to a `modern-critical-v1` profile was considered and rejected: `chronology()` and `tools/scripture-chronology` default to profile=None and return every profile's claims, so a second profile would leak the figure into ordinary queries until the tools filter by default - a tooling change outside this lane. This edit is a prerequisite of E1-010's `preferred`, because Sec. 4.4 forbids `preferred` beside `disputed`. Same event as E1-008, E1-010, LEAD-014, P-004; `old` strings disjoint. P-004 is satisfied by this edit and carries none of its own.

Howlett's 1020 is the same Egyptological reconstruction as the 1277 removed under E1-009, and being the ONLY claim on the subject it was what this profile answered for the founding of the monarchy. The correcting agent escalated it because the loader refused an event with an empty dates list and the event could not be deleted either - two bindings name it and four claims are measured from it. The lead made the smallest model change that lets the claim go: an event may hold no claim, asserting nothing and returning nothing, while a composition unit still requires one. The verses that narrate the accession now carry their book's composition chronology instead of a modern reconstruction.
